event.title: Typhoon Dolphin Strikes Japan, Heads Towards China with Preparations Underway
event.canonical_title: Typhoon Dolphin Strikes Japan, Heads Towards China with Preparations Underway
event.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has hit southern Japan, particularly affecting Okinawa, with maximum sustained winds of 162 km/h and gusts up to 216 km/h. The storm has caused injuries to five elderly individuals, primarily due to falls from strong winds. As the typhoon approaches China, ports have been closed in anticipation of its arrival.

timeline.title: Typhoon Dolphin Hits China's Eastern Coast with High Winds
timeline.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall on China's eastern coast, bringing sustained winds of up to 162 km/h. The storm is expected to continue affecting the region into Monday, with reports of over 1,600 flight cancellations and evacuations as residents prepare for the impact.

Sustained winds reached up to 162 km/h.
The storm is expected to continue into Monday.

timeline.title: Typhoon Dolphin Hits China, Causing Evacuations and Flight Cancellations
timeline.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall on China's east coast, becoming the strongest tropical cyclone to hit the country this year. The storm has prompted the evacuation of over one million people and led to numerous flight cancellations. Prior to reaching China, Typhoon Dolphin caused injuries and power outages in Japan's Okinawa province, affecting more than 50,000 buildings.
key_facts: Typhoon Dolphin made landfall on China's east coast.
It is the strongest tropical cyclone to hit China this year.
Over one million people have been evacuated.
The storm previously affected Japan's Okinawa province, injuring six people and cutting power to over 50,000 buildings.

event_overview.title: About Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.subject: Typhoon Dolphin
event_overview.summary: Typhoon Dolphin was the 13th named tropical cyclone of the 2026 western North Pacific season, forming in late July and later tracking westward across the region. It affected Japan’s Okinawa area before making landfall in Zhejiang province on China’s east coast; by August 10 it had weakened to a tropical storm inland.

facts.label: Formation and designation
facts.value: China’s National Meteorological Center designated Dolphin as 2026’s No. 13 typhoon; official reporting said it formed over the northwestern Pacific on July 27, 2026.

facts.label: China landfall and weakening
facts.value: Dolphin made landfall near Taizhou, Zhejiang, on the evening of August 9 with reported winds of 151 kph; on August 10, China’s National Meteorological Center listed it as a tropical storm over Dexing, Jiangxi, and forecast further weakening.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: “Dolphin” is a name contributed by Hong Kong, China, under the ESCAP/WMO Typhoon Committee naming list; it refers to the Chinese white dolphin and a Hong Kong mascot.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the August 8-10 Japan-to-China impact period and preparedness or disruption measures, not Dolphin’s full late-July development, its complete inland dissipation, or all effects elsewhere in the region.
